entries.seminar_title: Piece by Piece, Hour by Hour: Incentives, Productivity, and Turnover.
entries.speaker: Jared Grogan
entries.abstract: The choice of compensation method can affect employees’ effort levels, their selection into employment, and their human capital accumulation at a particular firm. However, in settings with especially high turnover, the costs of continually replacing employees may be substantial. We analyze a large group of employees paid primarily by piece rates but who are required to perform many tasks besides the one on which incentive payments are made. We explore whether a change in compensation scheme intended to leave mean earnings constant but that adds time-based compensation for the non-primary tasks can affect worker productivity and turnover. We use the staggered adoption of a new incentive contract for long distance truck drivers at a large American truckload motor carrier to perform a quasi-experimental analysis. We estimate effects on driving and non-driving work outcomes as well as the likelihood that drivers will quit over a given period of time. We discuss potential mechanisms behind the reported effects, and the costs and benefits of the compensation change that can be estimated with available data are reported and interpreted.

entries.seminar_title: Migration and the Supply of Hospitals
entries.speaker: Arjun Srinivasan
Udayan Vaidya
entries.abstract: A principal contracts with an agent through an informed delegate. Although the principal cannot directly mediate the interaction, she can restrict the menus of contracts the delegate may offer. We characterize the outcomes implementable through delegated contracting: they are exactly those achievable by a centralized Bayesian mechanism that is dominant-strategy incentive compatible and ex-post individually rational for the agent. We use this result to identify the optimal contractual restrictions in several settings. First, an organization that procures through a budget-indulgent agency should grant full flexibility below an expected spending cap. Second, unlike centralized mechanisms, delegated contracting can never dissolve partnerships efficiently, highlighting a limit to delegated authority. Finally, a seller can entrust sales to an intermediary without revenue loss by combining a resale price agreement with a buyback policy.
